shots.text: Meet Ada. Her homework is finished. The answer looks perfectly clear. But close the screen, and something changes.
shots.caption: The page is finished. Is the learning?
shots.purpose: Ada closes a completed answer and hesitates over an empty page.

shots.text: Does artificial intelligence help you learn, or just finish? The difference shows up when the help goes away.
shots.caption: What remains when the help goes away?
shots.purpose: Title opens from the empty answer circle; Ada presents the question.

shots.text: Finishing with help is one test. Doing it alone is another. Remembering later, and solving a different problem, are two more.
shots.caption: Help now. Alone. Later. Somewhere new.
shots.purpose: Four physical medallions expose four different outcome measures.

shots.text: In a randomized study of nearly a thousand high school mathematics students in Turkey, an unrestricted chatbot improved practice grades by forty eight percent, compared with the control group.
shots.caption: Practice grades: +48% relative to control.
shots.purpose: A Turkish classroom and a GPT-4 terminal establish the randomized study; the practice result stamps onto paper.

shots.text: But on the exam without the tool, that group scored seventeen percent lower. Better homework performance had hidden weaker independent performance.
shots.caption: Unaided exam grades: −17% relative to control.
shots.purpose: The screen is covered. A second test paper reveals the independent-performance reversal.

shots.text: A tutor designed around teacher supplied hints largely removed that penalty. It did not produce a statistically significant exam improvement over the control group.
shots.caption: Teacher-designed hints changed the outcome.
shots.purpose: The answer card becomes a hint card; show mitigation without inventing an exam gain.

shots.text: In a separate college physics experiment, a carefully designed tutor led to higher immediate test scores than an active classroom lesson.
shots.caption: Tutor design matters.
shots.purpose: A physics learner tests a pendulum with a structured tutor; establish a separate experiment.

shots.text: These are different designs and different settings. Neither result tells us what every learner will remember months later.
shots.caption: An immediate test is not a long-term test.
shots.purpose: A moving calendar and clock distinguish immediate testing from later memory.

shots.text: So, when learning is the goal, give the tool a different job. Let it support the thinking you need to practise.
shots.caption: Keep the thinking you need to practise.
shots.purpose: Ada moves the terminal aside to put her own working sheet in the centre.

shots.text: Step one. Make an attempt. If you know enough to start, put your own first step on the page.
shots.caption: Step one. Make an attempt.
shots.purpose: First numbered medallion; Ada writes her own attempt.

shots.text: For a completely new topic, study a clear worked example first. A beginner needs guidance, not a guessing contest.
shots.caption: New topic? Start with a worked example.
shots.purpose: Open example book supports a novice without pretending unassisted struggle is always best.

shots.text: Now ask for a hint about the exact step you cannot explain. Ask it to check your reasoning before showing the whole solution.
shots.caption: Ask for the next useful hint.
shots.purpose: Round detail callout shows the specific hint request and a partial response.

shots.text: Ada needs to solve two times a number, plus three, equals eleven. Her hint is simple: undo the addition first.
shots.caption: Undo the addition first.
shots.purpose: Close-up of the actual algebra and subtraction action.

shots.text: Step two. Hide the answer. Close the screen. Take a fresh sheet, and explain the method from memory.
shots.caption: Step two. Hide the answer.
shots.purpose: Second numbered medallion; a large gloved hand shuts the computer.

shots.text: Ada subtracts three from both sides. Then she divides both sides by two. The number is four. Each step has a reason.
shots.caption: Explain why each step works.
shots.purpose: An overhead page reveals the reasoning one step at a time.

shots.text: Check the work. Put four back into the original equation. Two times four, plus three, is eleven. If something fails, correct it.
shots.caption: Check. Correct. Try again.
shots.purpose: Ada substitutes the result into the original equation and stamps a check.

shots.text: Step three. Change the problem. New numbers are a start. A new situation checks whether you can choose the method yourself.
shots.caption: Step three. Change the problem.
shots.purpose: Third numbered medallion; the algebra sheet becomes a shop problem.

shots.text: Two notebooks and a three dollar delivery fee cost fifteen dollars. What does one notebook cost? Ada has to build the equation before solving it.
shots.caption: Choose the method in a new situation.
shots.purpose: Two notebooks, a delivery tag and a receipt establish a real transfer example.

shots.text: Come back later for another fresh problem, without the tool. That checks retention separately from what feels easy right now.
shots.caption: Return later. Try without the tool.
shots.purpose: Calendar page turns; a clean question awaits Ada with the computer closed.

shots.text: Attempt with suitable guidance. Hide, explain, and check. Change the problem, then return later. Keep the next independent attempt in view.
shots.caption: Attempt. Explain. Check. Transfer. Return.
shots.purpose: Pull back from the detail into the three-step manual card.

shots.text: This is a practical check, not a universally proven recipe. The right amount of help depends on the learner and the task.
shots.caption: Match the help to the learner and the task.
shots.purpose: Tip ribbon makes the practical limits explicit.

shots.text: A finished page is useful. A skill you can use again is something more. What can you do when the answer is gone?
shots.caption: What can you do when the answer is gone?
shots.purpose: Return to Ada and a new successful page, then close into a circular end card.
Circular end title and source attribution.
